solution: Using \(e^{k\log x} = x^k\), the integrand becomes \(\dfrac{x^6 - x^5}{x^4 - x^3} = \dfrac{x^5(x - 1)}{x^3(x - 1)} = x^2\). Hence \(\displaystyle\int x^2\,dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

If \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{f(x)}{\log(\sin x)}\,dx = \log[\log \sin x] + c\), differentiate the right side: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\log[\log \sin x] = \dfrac{1}{\log \sin x}\cdot \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{\cot x}{\log \sin x}\). Comparing, \(f(x) = \cot x\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

\(\dfrac{\sin^2 x}{1 + \cos x} = \dfrac{1 - \cos^2 x}{1 + \cos x} = \dfrac{(1 - \cos x)(1 + \cos x)}{1 + \cos x} = 1 - \cos x\). Therefore \(\displaystyle\int (1 - \cos x)\,dx = x - \sin x + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Since \(f''(x) = g''(x)\), the function \(f'(x) - g'(x)\) is constant, equal to \(f'(1) - g'(1) = 4 - 6 = -2\). Integrating, \(f(x) - g(x) = -2x + k\). At \(x = 2\): \(f(2) - g(2) = 3 - 9 = -6 = -4 + k\), so \(k = -2\). Then \(f(1) - g(1) = -2 + (-2) = -4\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Differentiate \(\displaystyle\int f(x)\,dx = \dfrac{f(x)}{2} + C\): we get \(f(x) = \dfrac{f'(x)}{2}\), i.e. \(f'(x) = 2f(x)\). The solution of this differential equation is \(f(x) = e^{2x}\) (an exponential, no additive constant). Matches option D. Hence (D).

Differentiate \(-\log(\log \cos x) + C\): \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[-\log(\log \cos x)] = -\dfrac{1}{\log \cos x}\cdot\dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x} = \dfrac{\tan x}{\log \cos x}\). Comparing with \(\dfrac{f(x)}{\log \cos x}\), \(f(x) = \tan x\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Since \(1 + \sin 2x = (\sin x + \cos x)^2\), \(\sqrt{1 + \sin 2x} = |\sin x + \cos x|\). The integrand equals \(\dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{|\sin x + \cos x|} = \pm 1\); taking the positive branch, \(I = \displaystyle\int 1\,dx = x\). Matches option C. Hence (C).
\(e^{x\log a} = a^x\), so the integrand is \(a^x e^x = (ae)^x\). Then \(\displaystyle\int (ae)^x\,dx = \dfrac{(ae)^x}{\log(ae)} + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Test option A: let \(f(x) = \dfrac{2}{(b^2 - a^2)\cos 2x}\). Then \(\log f(x) = \log 2 - \log(b^2 - a^2) - \log(\cos 2x)\), so \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{2(b^2 - a^2)}\log f(x)\right] = \dfrac{1}{2(b^2 - a^2)}\cdot 2\tan 2x = \dfrac{\tan 2x}{b^2 - a^2}\). The integrand \(f(x)\sin x \cos x = \dfrac{2}{(b^2 - a^2)\cos 2x}\cdot\dfrac{\sin 2x}{2} = \dfrac{\tan 2x}{b^2 - a^2}\), which matches. Hence (A).
By definition of the derivative, \(f(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin^2 x) = 2\sin x\cos x = \sin 2x\). Then \(\displaystyle\int 4f(x)\,dx = \int 4\sin 2x\,dx = -2\cos 2x + c\). Matches option D. Hence (D).

\(\dfrac{2^{x+1} - 5^{x-1}}{10^x} = 2\cdot\dfrac{2^x}{10^x} - \dfrac{1}{5}\cdot\dfrac{5^x}{10^x} = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^x - \dfrac{1}{5}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^x\). Integrating: \(\displaystyle\int 2\,(1/5)^x\,dx = \dfrac{-2}{\log 5}5^{-x}\) and \(\displaystyle\int -\tfrac{1}{5}(1/2)^x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{5\log 2}2^{-x}\). Sum \(= \dfrac{-2}{\log 5}5^{-x} + \dfrac{1}{5\log 2}2^{-x} + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).
Differentiate \(\dfrac{1}{2}f^2(x) + c\): we get \(f(x)f'(x)\). Comparing with the integrand \(f(x)\cos x\), we need \(f'(x) = \cos x\), so \(f(x) = \sin x\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(1 + \cos 8x = 2\cos^2 4x\), so \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{2\cos^2 4x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \sec^2 4x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\tan 4x}{4} = \dfrac{\tan 4x}{8} + C\). Matches option D. Hence (D).

\(\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x = (\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x)^3 - 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = 1 - 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x\). Therefore the integrand \(= 1 - 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x + 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x = 1\). Hence \(\displaystyle\int 1\,dx = x + c\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

\(\cos 2x - \cos 2\theta = (2\cos^2 x - 1) - (2\cos^2\theta - 1) = 2(\cos^2 x - \cos^2\theta) = 2(\cos x - \cos\theta)(\cos x + \cos\theta)\). Dividing by \(\cos x - \cos\theta\) gives \(2(\cos x + \cos\theta)\). Then \(\displaystyle\int 2(\cos x + \cos\theta)\,dx = 2(\sin x + x\cos\theta) + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

\(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9 - 16x^2}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{4}\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(3/4)^2 - x^2}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{4}\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}\right) + c\). So \(\alpha = \dfrac{1}{4}\) and \(\beta = \dfrac{4}{3}\), giving \(\alpha + \dfrac{1}{\beta} = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} = 1\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

\(\sqrt{\dfrac{x - 5}{x - 7}} = \dfrac{x - 5}{\sqrt{(x - 5)(x - 7)}} = \dfrac{x - 5}{\sqrt{x^2 - 12x + 35}}\). Write \(x - 5 = \tfrac{1}{2}(2x - 12) + 1\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\tfrac{1}{2}(2x - 12)}{\sqrt{x^2 - 12x + 35}}\,dx = \sqrt{x^2 - 12x + 35}\) and \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x - 6)^2 - 1}}\,dx = \log\left|x - 6 + \sqrt{x^2 - 12x + 35}\right|\). Thus the coefficient \(A = 1\). Matches option D. Hence (D).

Let \(u = \log(\sec x - \tan x)\). Then \(du = \dfrac{\sec x\tan x - \sec^2 x}{\sec x - \tan x}\,dx = \dfrac{-\sec x(\sec x - \tan x)}{\sec x - \tan x}\,dx = -\sec x\,dx\), so \(\sec x\,dx = -du\). Hence \(\displaystyle\int u(-du) = -\dfrac{u^2}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\{\log(\sec x - \tan x)\}^2 + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Let \(u = e^x \cdot x\). Then \(du = (e^x + e^x x)\,dx = e^x(1 + x)\,dx\). The integral becomes \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{du}{\cos^2 u} = \int \sec^2 u\,du = \tan u + c = \tan(e^x \cdot x) + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(\tan^3 x + \tan x = \tan x(\tan^2 x + 1) = \tan x\sec^2 x\), so the integrand is \(\sec^m x\cdot\tan x\sec^2 x = \sec^{m+1} x\,(\sec x\tan x)\). With \(u = \sec x,\ du = \sec x\tan x\,dx\), \(\displaystyle\int u^{m+1}\,du = \dfrac{u^{m+2}}{m + 2} = \dfrac{\sec^{m+2} x}{m + 2} + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).
\(\dfrac{1}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x}\). With \(u = \tan x,\ du = \sec^2 x\,dx\), \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{du}{u} = \log|u| = \log|\tan x| + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Let \(u = x + \tan^{-1} x\). Then \(du = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\right)dx = \dfrac{x^2 + 2}{x^2 + 1}\,dx\). The integral becomes \(\displaystyle\int a^u\,du = \dfrac{a^u}{\log a} = \dfrac{a^{x + \tan^{-1} x}}{\log a} + c\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Let \(u = \log\!\left(\dfrac{g(x)}{f(x)}\right) = \log g(x) - \log f(x)\). Then \(du = \left(\dfrac{g'}{g} - \dfrac{f'}{f}\right)dx = \dfrac{fg' - f'g}{fg}\,dx\). The integral is \(\displaystyle\int u\,du = \dfrac{u^2}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\log\!\left(\dfrac{g(x)}{f(x)}\right)\right]^2 + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Take \(x^4\) out of \((x^4 + 1)^{3/4}\): denominator \(= x^2\cdot x^3(1 + x^{-4})^{3/4} = x^5(1 + x^{-4})^{3/4}\). So the integral is \(\displaystyle\int x^{-5}(1 + x^{-4})^{-3/4}\,dx\). Let \(u = 1 + x^{-4},\ du = -4x^{-5}\,dx\); then \(\displaystyle\int -\tfrac{1}{4}u^{-3/4}\,du = -u^{1/4} = -\left(\dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^4}\right)^{1/4} + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\sin^3 x\cos x}} = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan^{3/2} x}\) (divide numerator and denominator by \(\cos^2 x\)). With \(u = \tan x,\ du = \sec^2 x\,dx\), \(\displaystyle\int u^{-3/2}\,du = \dfrac{u^{-1/2}}{-1/2} = \dfrac{-2}{\sqrt{\tan x}} + c\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Let \(\theta = \sin^{-1} x\), so \(d\theta = \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\). The integral becomes \(\displaystyle\int \sec^2\theta\,d\theta = \tan\theta + c = \tan(\sin^{-1} x) + c\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} = 1 - \dfrac{e^x}{1 + e^x}\), so \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x}\,dx = x - \log(1 + e^x) + C\). Since \(x - \log(1 + e^x) = x - \log[e^x(1 + e^{-x})] = -\log(1 + e^{-x})\), the answer is \(-\log(1 + e^{-x}) + C\). Matches option D. Hence (D).

\(\dfrac{\cos^{n-1} x}{\sin^{n+1} x} = \dfrac{\cos^{n-1} x}{\sin^{n-1} x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \cot^{n-1} x\,\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\). With \(u = \cot x,\ du = -\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\,dx\), \(\displaystyle\int u^{n-1}(-du) = -\dfrac{u^n}{n} = \dfrac{-\cot^n x}{n} + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(e^x\): \(\dfrac{e^x(\sin x + \cos x)}{1 + e^x\sin x}\). The numerator equals \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(1 + e^x\sin x) = e^x\sin x + e^x\cos x\). Hence the integral is \(\log|1 + e^x\sin x| + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Write \(\cos x = \tfrac{1}{2}[(\sin x + \cos x) + (\cos x - \sin x)]\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int 1\,dx + \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}[x + \log|\sin x + \cos x|] + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Let \(u = 3^x,\ du = 3^x\ln 3\,dx\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{3^x}{\sqrt{1 - (3^x)^2}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{\log 3}\int \dfrac{du}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\log 3}\sin^{-1}(3^x) + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Let \(u = \log(\log x)\). Then \(du = \dfrac{1}{\log x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{x\log x}\,dx\). The integral becomes \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{du}{u} = \log|u| = \log|\log(\log x)| + C\). Matches option D. Hence (D).
\(\frac{d}{dx}\left[x\,e^{x+1/x}\right]=e^{x+1/x}\left(1+x-\frac1x\right)\), exactly the integrand, so the integral is \(x\,e^{x+1/x}+C\). Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\sin 2x} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{2\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{2\tan x\cos^2 x} = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{2\sqrt{\tan x}}\). With \(u = \tan x,\ du = \sec^2 x\,dx\), \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{du}{2\sqrt{u}} = \sqrt{u} = \sqrt{\tan x} + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

\(\dfrac{\sqrt{\cot x}}{\sin x\cos x} = \sqrt{\cot x}\cdot\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\cdot\tan x = \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\,\cot^{-1/2} x\). With \(u = \cot x,\ du = -\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\,dx\), \(\displaystyle\int u^{-1/2}(-du) = -2u^{1/2} = -2\sqrt{\cot x}\). Thus \(P = -2\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Put \(t = \tan(x/2)\), so \(\cos x = \dfrac{1 - t^2}{1 + t^2}\) and \(dx = \dfrac{2}{1 + t^2}\,dt\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{5 + 4\cos x} = \int \dfrac{2}{5(1 + t^2) + 4(1 - t^2)}\,dt = \int \dfrac{2}{9 + t^2}\,dt = \dfrac{2}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{t}{3}\). So \(P = \dfrac{2}{3}\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Numerator \(\sin^8 x - \cos^8 x = (\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x)(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x) = (\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x)\), and \(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\cos^2 x\). Dividing by the denominator gives \(\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x = -\cos 2x\). Hence \(\displaystyle\int -\cos 2x\,dx = -\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Put \(x = t^2,\ dx = 2t\,dt,\ \sqrt{x} = t\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{t}{t^2(t^2 + 1)}\cdot 2t\,dt = \int \dfrac{2}{t^2 + 1}\,dt = 2\tan^{-1} t = 2\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\). So \(k = 2,\ m = \sqrt{x}\), i.e. \((2, \sqrt{x})\). Matches option C. Hence (C).
Put \(u=\log(x+\sqrt{1+x^2})\), so \(du=\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\). The integral becomes \(\int u\,du=\tfrac12\left[\log(x+\sqrt{1+x^2})\right]^2+C\). Hence (C).

Numerator \(x^{e-1} + e^{x-1} = \dfrac{1}{e}(e\,x^{e-1} + e^x) = \dfrac{1}{e}\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^e + e^x)\). Hence \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^{e-1} + e^{x-1}}{x^e + e^x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{e}\log(x^e + e^x) + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2(x/2)\), so \(\sqrt{1 + \cos x} = \sqrt{2}\,\cos(x/2)\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \sqrt{2}\cos(x/2)\,dx = \sqrt{2}\cdot 2\sin(x/2) = 2\sqrt{2}\sin\dfrac{x}{2} + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Put \(t = \sqrt{1 - x}\), so \(x = 1 - t^2,\ dx = -2t\,dt\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{(1 - t^2)^2}{t}(-2t)\,dt = -2\int (1 - 2t^2 + t^4)\,dt = -2\!\left[t - \dfrac{2t^3}{3} + \dfrac{t^5}{5}\right]\). Factoring \(-2t\) and substituting \(t^2 = 1 - x\), the bracket simplifies to \(\dfrac{3x^2 + 4x + 8}{15}\). Thus the integral \(= -\dfrac{2}{15}\sqrt{1 - x}\,(3x^2 + 4x + 8)\), so \(P = -\dfrac{2}{15}\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Let \(u = 5^{5^{5^x}}\). Differentiating, \(\dfrac{du}{dx} = 5^{5^{5^x}}\cdot 5^{5^x}\cdot 5^x\,(\log 5)^3\). Hence the integrand equals \(\dfrac{1}{(\log 5)^3}\,du\), and \(\displaystyle\int = \dfrac{u}{(\log 5)^3} = \dfrac{5^{5^{5^x}}}{(\log 5)^3} + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Write \(\sin x = \sin((x - \alpha) + \alpha) = \sin(x - \alpha)\cos\alpha + \cos(x - \alpha)\sin\alpha\). Then \(\dfrac{\sin x}{\sin(x - \alpha)} = \cos\alpha + \sin\alpha\cot(x - \alpha)\), so \(\displaystyle\int = x\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha\log|\sin(x - \alpha)| + K\). Thus \(A = \cos\alpha,\ B = \sin\alpha\), and \(A - B = \cos\alpha - \sin\alpha\). At \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(A - B = 0 - 1 = -1\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Let \(u = \log(\tan x)\). Then \(du = \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{\sin x\cos x}\,dx\). The integral becomes \(\displaystyle\int u\,du = \dfrac{u^2}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}(\log_e\tan x)^2 + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Put \(x = \cos\theta\), so \(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\theta}{1 + \cos\theta} = \tan^2(\theta/2)\) and \(\sqrt{\cdot} = \tan(\theta/2)\). Then \(\tan^{-1}(\tan(\theta/2)) = \theta/2\), and \(\cos\{2\cdot\theta/2\} = \cos\theta = x\). Hence the integral \(= \displaystyle\int x\,dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + c\). Matches option D. Hence (D).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(x^2\): \(\dfrac{1 + 1/x^2}{x^2 - 1 + 1/x^2}\). Let \(u = x - \dfrac{1}{x},\ du = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)dx\); the denominator becomes \(u^2 + 1\). So \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{du}{u^2 + 1} = \tan^{-1} u = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x^2 - 1}{x}\right) + c\). Matches option D. Hence (D).
Complete the square: \(8 + 2x - x^2 = 9 - (x - 1)^2\). Then \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9 - (x - 1)^2}}\,dx = \sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{3}\right) + c\). Matches option D. Hence (D).

This is the standard form \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^2 - x^2}}\,dx = \sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\) with \(a = \sqrt{7}\). Hence \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{7 - x^2}}\,dx = \sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{7}}\right) + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(x^2 + x - 2 = (x + 2)(x - 1)\). Partial fractions: \(\dfrac{1}{(x + 2)(x - 1)} = \dfrac{1}{3}\!\left[\dfrac{1}{x - 1} - \dfrac{1}{x + 2}\right]\). Integrating, \(\dfrac{1}{3}\log\left|\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 2}\right| + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

Multiply \(J\) top and bottom by \(e^{4x}\): \(J = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^{3x}}{e^{4x} + e^{2x} + 1}\,dx\). Then \(J - I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^x(e^{2x} - 1)}{e^{4x} + e^{2x} + 1}\,dx\). With \(t = e^x\), this is \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{t^2 - 1}{t^4 + t^2 + 1}\,dt\); dividing by \(t^2\) and putting \(u = t + \tfrac{1}{t}\) gives \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{du}{u^2 - 1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{u - 1}{u + 1}\right| = \dfrac{1}{2}\log\!\left(\dfrac{e^{2x} - e^x + 1}{e^{2x} + e^x + 1}\right) + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{x^2 + 1}{x^2 - 1} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{x^2 - 1}\). Then \(\displaystyle\int 1\,dx + 2\int \dfrac{dx}{x^2 - 1} = x + 2\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right| = x + \log\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Partial fractions in \(x^2\): \(\dfrac{1}{(x^2 + 4)(x^2 + 9)} = \dfrac{1}{5}\!\left[\dfrac{1}{x^2 + 4} - \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 9}\right]\). Integrating: \(\dfrac{1}{5}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{5}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{3}\), so \(A = \dfrac{1}{10},\ B = -\dfrac{1}{15}\). Then \(A - B = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 + 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{6}\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Write \(\dfrac{3x - 2}{(x + 3)(x + 1)^2} = \dfrac{A}{x + 3} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1} + \dfrac{C}{(x + 1)^2}\). At \(x = -3\): \(-11 = 4A \Rightarrow A = -\tfrac{11}{4}\). At \(x = -1\): \(-5 = 2C \Rightarrow C = -\tfrac{5}{2}\). Matching \(x^2\): \(0 = A + B \Rightarrow B = \tfrac{11}{4}\). Integrating: \(-\tfrac{11}{4}\log|x + 3| + \tfrac{11}{4}\log|x + 1| + \tfrac{5}{2(x + 1)} = \dfrac{11}{4}\log\left|\dfrac{x + 1}{x + 3}\right| + \dfrac{5}{2(x + 1)} + C\). Matches option D. Hence (D).
\(\dfrac{1}{x(x + 1)} = \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\). Integrating, \(\log|x| - \log|x + 1| = \log\left|\dfrac{x}{x + 1}\right| + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(\dfrac{x + 3}{(x + 4)^2} = \dfrac{(x + 4) - 1}{(x + 4)^2} = \dfrac{1}{x + 4} - \dfrac{1}{(x + 4)^2}\). With \(f = \dfrac{1}{x + 4},\ f' = -\dfrac{1}{(x + 4)^2}\), the integral is of the form \(\displaystyle\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^x f = \dfrac{e^x}{x + 4} + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

Integrating by parts twice (or using the standard result), \(\displaystyle\int \cos(\log x)\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2}[\cos(\log x) + \sin(\log x)] + c\). So \(F(x) = \dfrac{x}{2}[\cos(\log x) + \sin(\log x)]\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

By parts, \(\displaystyle\int \log(a^2 + x^2)\,dx = x\log(a^2 + x^2) - \int \dfrac{2x^2}{a^2 + x^2}\,dx = x\log(a^2 + x^2) - 2\int\!\left(1 - \dfrac{a^2}{a^2 + x^2}\right)dx = x\log(a^2 + x^2) - 2x + 2a\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)\). So \(h(x) = x\log(a^2 + x^2) - 2x + 2a\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(1 + \cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x\), so the integrand \(= \dfrac{2x + 2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x} = x\sec^2 x + \tan x\). Now \(\displaystyle\int x\sec^2 x\,dx = x\tan x - \int \tan x\,dx\), and adding the remaining \(\displaystyle\int \tan x\,dx\) cancels it, leaving \(x\tan x + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

Write \(\dfrac{x^2 + 1}{(x + 1)^2} = \dfrac{(x^2 - 1) + 2}{(x + 1)^2} = \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1} + \dfrac{2}{(x + 1)^2}\). With \(f = \dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1},\ f' = \dfrac{2}{(x + 1)^2}\), the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^x f = e^x\!\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{1 + \sin x}{1 + \cos x} = \dfrac{1 + 2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}{2\cos^2(x/2)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2(x/2) + \tan(x/2)\). With \(f = \tan(x/2),\ f' = \dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2(x/2)\), the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^x\tan(x/2) + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{2 + \sin x}{1 + \cos x} = \dfrac{2}{2\cos^2(x/2)} + \dfrac{2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}{2\cos^2(x/2)} = \sec^2(x/2) + \tan(x/2)\). Since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\!\left[e^{x/2}\tan(x/2)\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}e^{x/2}[\tan(x/2) + \sec^2(x/2)]\), we get \(\displaystyle\int e^{x/2}[\sec^2(x/2) + \tan(x/2)]\,dx = 2e^{x/2}\tan\dfrac{x}{2} + C\). Matches option A. Hence (A).

\(\dfrac{x - 1}{(x + 1)^3} = \dfrac{(x + 1) - 2}{(x + 1)^3} = \dfrac{1}{(x + 1)^2} - \dfrac{2}{(x + 1)^3}\). With \(f = \dfrac{1}{(x + 1)^2},\ f' = -\dfrac{2}{(x + 1)^3}\), the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^x f = \dfrac{e^x}{(x + 1)^2} + C\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(\dfrac{x}{(1 + x)^2} = \dfrac{(1 + x) - 1}{(1 + x)^2} = \dfrac{1}{1 + x} - \dfrac{1}{(1 + x)^2}\). With \(g = \dfrac{1}{1 + x},\ g' = -\dfrac{1}{(1 + x)^2}\), \(\displaystyle\int e^x(g + g')\,dx = e^x g = \dfrac{e^x}{1 + x}\). So \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x}\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{e^x}{x}(x\log x + 1) = e^x\!\left(\log x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)\). With \(f = \log x,\ f' = \dfrac{1}{x}\), the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^x\log x = e^x\log|x| + C\). Matches option C. Hence (C).

\(\dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{1 - \sin^2 x} = \dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{\cos^2 x} = \sec x\tan x + \sec x\). With \(f = \sec x,\ f' = \sec x\tan x\), the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^x\sec x + c\). Matches option C. Hence (C).
By parts, \(\displaystyle\int \sin^{-1} x\,dx = x\sin^{-1} x - \int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx = x\sin^{-1} x + \sqrt{1 - x^2} + c\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

By parts, \(\displaystyle\int (\log x)^2\,dx = x(\log x)^2 - 2x\log x + 2x + C = x(\log x)^2 - 2x(\log x - 1) + C\). Comparing with \(x[f(x)]^2 + Ax[f(x) - 1]\): \(f(x) = \log x\) and \(Ax(\log x - 1) = -2x(\log x - 1)\), so \(A = -2\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

\(f(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^x (t^2 + t + 1)\,dt = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^2}{2} + x\). Since \(f'(x) = x^2 + x + 1 > 0\), \(f\) is increasing on \([2, 3]\). Maximum at \(x = 3\): \(9 + \tfrac{9}{2} + 3 = \tfrac{33}{2}\); minimum at \(x = 2\): \(\tfrac{8}{3} + 2 + 2 = \tfrac{20}{3}\). Difference \(= \tfrac{33}{2} - \tfrac{20}{3} = \dfrac{99 - 40}{6} = \dfrac{59}{6}\). Matches option C. Hence (C).
